summary.text: Beth Farnham is the Democratic nominee for Pennsylvania's 13th District. A former credit analyst, pharmacy technician and Conewago Valley school board member who describes herself as a stay-at-home parent, she also ran against John Joyce in 2024. Her campaign materials emphasize democracy, reproductive freedom, affordability, universal health care and gun safety.

paragraphs.text: Beth Farnham grew up in Maryland and graduated from Annapolis Senior High School.
Her campaign website says she is the child of an HVAC technician and a nurse, spent most of her childhood in a row home in Baltimore and attended public schools.
She earned an associate degree from Anne Arundel Community College in 1992 and a bachelor's degree from Towson University in 1996.
Her campaign website describes her degree as Biology, French and Secondary Education and says she put herself through college as the only member of her immediate family to graduate.

Farnham worked her way through college as a pharmacy technician, including at a fertility pharmacy, and later worked as an administrative assistant for a lift-equipment company and as a credit analyst for Bank of America, according to a 2024 WPSU interview.
She describes herself as a stay-at-home parent (13 years as of her 2024 interview).
She says she and her husband, Rob, were Republicans before moving toward the Democratic Party after 2016, and that she registered as a Democrat in 2019.
Farnham served on the Conewago Valley School District board, representing Region 2, and left office in 2023.
She won the 2024 Democratic primary with 98.8% of the vote and lost the general election to Joyce, 25.8% to 74.1%.

Unopposed in the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary (32,428 votes), she is running a second time against Joyce, and the Altoona Mirror reports her platform includes raising the federal minimum wage, a national health care plan and reproductive-freedom legislation.

According to her campaign website, she and her husband married at Gettysburg Presbyterian Church, settled in Adams County and are raising their children there; Ballotpedia lists her residence as Conewago Township.
